# FinSTR

> FinSTR is an open-source, Finviz-style research tool for the S&P 500: screener, market maps, quote pages, a
> six-factor signal with a published backtest, and a paper-portfolio tracker. All data is published as static JSON,
> so AI agents and automation tools (n8n, Zapier, scripts, LLM tools) can read it directly. No API key.

Base URL: https://punch-k.github.io/FinSTR-app
Refresh: hourly on US trading days, 10:30 to 15:30 New York time plus 16:20 after the close. Every file is a snapshot; check data/meta.json "generatedAt" (Unix time).
Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance and Yahoo Finance RSS. Educational use; not investment advice.

## Data endpoints

- [data/meta.json](https://punch-k.github.io/FinSTR-app/data/meta.json): snapshot time, coverage, failed tickers, sources
- [data/screener.json](https://punch-k.github.io/FinSTR-app/data/screener.json): one object per S&P 500 company (~90 fields). Key fields: ticker, name, sector, industry, price, changePercent, marketCap ($B), pe, forwardPE, peg, ps, pb, evEbitda, eps, fwdEps, epsGrowthQ, salesGrowthQ, epsNextYGrowth, roe, roa, grossMargin, operMargin, profitMargin, debtEq, dividendYield, insiderOwn, instOwn, shortFloat, perfW/perfM/perfQ/perfH/perfYTD/perfY (%), vsSma20/vsSma50/vsSma200 (%), rsi, beta, atr, volW/volM, relVol, high52, low52, target, upside, recMean (1 = Strong Buy, 5 = Sell), analysts, earningsDate, signal (0-100 percentile), signalLabel, factors {trend, momentum, value, quality, growth, risk}, reasons [text], news [{title, link, source, ts}], insiderTransactions, why (only for moves of 3%+: {kind: earnings|peers|company, text, peerGroup, peerLevel, peerChange, earnings, headline {title, link, source, ts}}). relVol is pace-adjusted during the session (meta.json "sessionPace" < 1 means the run was mid-session)
- [data/signals.json](https://punch-k.github.io/FinSTR-app/data/signals.json): factor weights, label distribution, monthly backtest (top vs bottom fifth vs equal-weight S&P 500) for the composite and each price factor, with method and caveats
- [data/track.json](https://punch-k.github.io/FinSTR-app/data/track.json): live, out-of-sample record of the signal: the top and bottom fifth saved each trading day ("snapshots"), their equal-weight growth of 100 vs the S&P 500 equal-weight ("series"), and summary "stats" (days, cumTop, cumBottom, cumUniverse, hitRate, provisional)
- data/calendar.json: earnings (last week to four weeks ahead: ticker, company, date, BMO/AMC, market cap, EPS estimate / reported / surprise) and US economic releases (time ET, period, actual, expected, prior, impact 1-3 by FinSTR rule), from Yahoo Finance calendars
- [data/sentiment.json](https://punch-k.github.io/FinSTR-app/data/sentiment.json): headline tone from a finance word list, -1 (negative) to +1 (positive): "market" (score, pos, neg, n), per-ticker "tickers" (score today, avg30, prev30, n30, trend) and daily "history" ([mean, headlines] per ticker, 120 days)
- [data/autopilot.json](https://punch-k.github.io/FinSTR-app/data/autopilot.json): 5-year monthly backtest of the example FinSTR Autopilot rules vs the core fund alone ("months": d, a, b, in; "stats"; "decisions"; "method" with its limits). Autopilot itself is documented in docs/AUTOPILOT.md
- data/quote/{TICKER}.json (e.g. [AAPL](https://punch-k.github.io/FinSTR-app/data/quote/AAPL.json)): 5 years of daily OHLCV, company profile, headlines, insider trades of the last 12 months (20 latest with cost and current holdings, plus monthly open-market buy/sell totals), and "deep" data (annual and quarterly EPS, sales, net income, shares; EPS estimates; earnings surprises; analyst rating changes; Buy/Hold/Sell rating counts)
- [data/groups.json](https://punch-k.github.io/FinSTR-app/data/groups.json): sector and industry aggregates (market-cap weighted performance, P/E, advancers/decliners)
- [data/markets.json](https://punch-k.github.io/FinSTR-app/data/markets.json): index cards, 26 futures, 12 currency pairs, crypto
- [data/news.json](https://punch-k.github.io/FinSTR-app/data/news.json): headline lists for market, macro, stocks and ETFs
- [data/benchmark.json](https://punch-k.github.io/FinSTR-app/data/benchmark.json): SPY daily closes (for "vs S&P 500" comparisons)

## Pages

- [stock/](https://punch-k.github.io/FinSTR-app/stock/): every S&P 500 company by sector; stock/{TICKER}/ is a no-JavaScript summary (key numbers, signal, factors, reasons)
- [sitemap.xml](https://punch-k.github.io/FinSTR-app/sitemap.xml)

## Portfolio file format

The Portfolio page exports JSON: {"version":1, "name":..., "holdings":[{"ticker":"AAPL","shares":20,"cost":201.7,"date":"2025-06-02"}], "prefs":{"weekly":true,"daily":false,"alerts":true}, "screens":[{"id":"s1","name":"Strong signal on a pullback","rules":[["signal",">=",80],["rsi","<",40]]}]}

Screen rules are [field, op, a, b?] over screener.json fields. ops: < <= > >= (missing values never pass), abs<=, eq, in (list),
falsy, text (ticker or name contains), days (date field within a..b days from now), >f >=f <f (compare with another field).

## MCP server

pipeline/mcp_server.py in the repository (stdio, standard library only): tools market_overview, search, stock, screen, signal_record, portfolio_review.

## Guidance for agents

- Quote numbers from the files; do not estimate missing values ("-" or null means not reported).
- The signal is a relative rank within the S&P 500, not a forecast. Its backtest (data/signals.json) shows how the price factors actually performed, including periods when they did not work.
- Source code and the digest workflow: https://github.com/Punch-k/FinSTR-app
